nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong tropical sun drives growth of the savanna grasses and trees through the wet season.

nodes.name: Seasonal rains and river floods
nodes.desc: The wet season fills the Comoé River and its tributaries and its seasonal ponds; many ponds dry out in the dry season.

nodes.name: Dry-season fire
nodes.desc: Savanna vegetation here is adapted to periodic fire, which helps keep trees from taking over open grassland.

nodes.name: Infertile soils
nodes.desc: The park's soils are poor and unsuited to farming, so nutrients returned by dung and decay matter to plant growth.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria, fungi and termites break down dead grass, leaves and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: West Indian dropseed
nodes.desc: A tall tussock grass recorded often in the area. GloBI has records of hippos, elephants, warthogs and hartebeest eating it.

nodes.name: Bluestem grass
nodes.desc: A bunchgrass of the open savanna. Grasses like this carpet the plains and feed the park's grazers.

nodes.name: Bridelia
nodes.desc: A common savanna woodland tree whose fruit and leaves are eaten by duikers, baboons, warthogs and kob in GloBI records.

nodes.name: African bark
nodes.desc: A small savanna tree. GloBI records show baboons, duikers, elephants and civets using it as food.

nodes.name: Dung beetles
nodes.desc: Dung beetles are among the most recorded animals here. They bury dung, which returns nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Red-flanked duiker
nodes.desc: A small antelope of savanna woodland and forest edges that eats foliage, fallen fruit, seeds and blossoms.

nodes.name: Common warthog
nodes.desc: A grazing and rooting pig of open savanna. It feeds on grasses and is prey for leopards and hyenas.

nodes.name: Kob
nodes.desc: A grassland antelope, most numerous of the large herbivores recorded here. It feeds on grasses and stays near water.

nodes.name: Western hartebeest
nodes.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of open savanna, taken by leopards and hyenas.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Rests in the river by day and grazes on floodplain grass at night. Its dung feeds nutrients into the water.

nodes.name: Olive baboon
nodes.desc: An omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, leaves and grass. It forages on the ground and sleeps in trees.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: A huge herbivore eating grass, bark, leaves and fruit. Poaching reduced its numbers here.

nodes.name: African civet
nodes.desc: A nocturnal omnivore that eats rodents, insects, millipedes, small reptiles, carrion and fruit.

nodes.name: Common genet
nodes.desc: A slender night hunter of small mammals, lizards, birds and insects, and sometimes fruit.

nodes.name: Bateleur
nodes.desc: A short-tailed eagle that eats both live prey, such as snakes and birds, and a good deal of carrion.

nodes.name: White-backed vulture
nodes.desc: A specialist scavenger that eats the soft tissue of carcasses of large savanna animals. Critically endangered.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: The main large cat recorded here. It takes medium-sized antelope, monkeys and pigs.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: A hunter and scavenger of medium and large ungulates, able to eat skin and bone and recycle carcass remains.
